title: Rising demand, lower price than competitors to boost rice exports: IREF
description:
India's rice exports have risen 13 per cent in value terms during the first half of this fiscal year, and the outlook remains strong as the country has surplus stock to meet rising global demand, according to the industry body IREF.
In an interview with PTI, Indian Rice Exporters Federation (IREF) Vice President Dev Gard said the price of Indian rice is at least 10 per cent cheaper than competitors.
According to government data, India's rice exports grew 13 per cent to Rs 54,937.71 crore in the first six months of this fiscal year. India produced over 154 million tonnes of rice in the 2025-26 crop year ending in June.
"Indian rice prices are at an all-time low. Our export prices are almost 10 per cent cheaper than the second alternative available in the market, that is Thailand or Myanmar," Garg said.
The global demand is also expected to rise because of the likely fall in production amid El Nino threat, he added.
